strong.text: You came through with no gaps in the core areas. You separated what a stem asks from what the old key says, and that habit carries thyroid questions. Use the review cards for any item marked below, and revisit the module in a week to check it holds.

mixed.text: You have a workable base and some real gaps. Each fall below names the model to fix, not something you cannot do. Start with the confident errors, then the gaps, then the shaky items, and retake the module after those review cards.

weak.text: Several core areas need rebuilding, and that gives you a clear order. Begin with the traps you fell into while Sure, then work the cards in the order listed, starting with the nodule work-up and how each cancer is diagnosed. Then retake the module.

secure.text: Secure: you asked whether the stem wants the first test or the test of choice. TSH and ultrasound come first; FNAC names the nodule.

shaky.text: Shaky: you know both tests but the order wobbled. Say it aloud: TSH and ultrasound first, scan only if TSH is low, FNAC for the nature of the nodule.

gap.text: Gap: first test and test of choice are still merged. TSH and ultrasound come first, a scan only if TSH is low, and FNAC tells you what the nodule is. Redo the work-up card first.

secure.text: Secure: you diagnose papillary by nuclei and follicular by invasion, and you know FNAC and frozen section cannot show invasion.

shaky.text: Shaky: the split mostly holds, but the nuclei-versus-invasion rule slipped on some stems. Ask which feature the tumour is defined by before reading the options.

gap.text: Gap: how each cancer is diagnosed is not holding. Papillary rests on nuclear features; follicular needs capsular or vascular invasion on histology, which FNAC cannot show. Review the papillary-versus-follicular card.

secure.text: Secure: you tied papillary to the 'most common' questions and moved to follicular only when iodine deficiency was stated.

shaky.text: Shaky: you know papillary leads, but some settings pulled you elsewhere. Check whether the stem says overall or relative, children, radiation or thyroglossal cyst.

gap.text: Gap: the 'most common' answers are not settled. Papillary is the commonest overall, in children, after radiation and in a thyroglossal cyst; follicular gains share only in iodine deficiency. Review that card.

secure.text: Secure: you matched route to tumour, with papillary in lymphatics and follicular in blood to lung and bone, and kept medullary and anaplastic out of DTC.

shaky.text: Shaky: the routes mostly hold, but a site or list slipped. Derive the route from the cell: follicular invades vessels, so it goes by blood.

gap.text: Gap: spread and set membership are not reliable. Papillary goes by lymphatics to neck nodes; follicular goes by blood to lung and bone, with nodes uncommon; medullary and anaplastic are not DTC. Review the spread card.

secure.text: Secure: you matched each Bethesda category to its action and kept II, IV and V apart.

shaky.text: Shaky: you know the categories but a name or action got swapped. Pair each number with its word, then its action.

gap.text: Gap: Bethesda category to action is not holding. II is follow-up, IV is diagnostic lobectomy or molecular testing, V and VI are cancer surgery. Review the Bethesda card.

secure.text: Secure: you chose the operation by size and risk, and you can give both the classic key and current practice.

shaky.text: Shaky: you know the size bands but some cases defaulted to one operation. Walk the ladder: under 1 cm, 1 to 4 cm, over 4 cm or advanced.

gap.text: Gap: the extent of surgery is still one answer for every case. PYQs expected total thyroidectomy; current guidance accepts lobectomy for low-risk 1 to 4 cm and lobectomy or surveillance below 1 cm. Review the surgery ladder card.

secure.text: Secure: you gave radioiodine by risk, raised TSH before the dose and matched suppression to risk afterwards.

shaky.text: Shaky: the radioiodine logic mostly holds, but one phase blurred. Keep the phases apart: high TSH to drive uptake, then suppression to starve residual tumour.

gap.text: Gap: radioiodine and TSH are not holding. It is not routine for low risk, it needs a high TSH to be taken up, and suppression comes afterwards, deeper for high risk. Review the radioiodine card.

secure.text: Secure: you paired thyroglobulin with DTC and calcitonin with medullary, and you doubted Tg when antibodies or a negative scan complicated it.

shaky.text: Shaky: you know the markers but the interpretation wobbled. Check antibodies before trusting Tg, and switch tests when iodine uptake is lost.

gap.text: Gap: follow-up markers are not reliable yet. Thyroglobulin follows DTC, calcitonin follows medullary, antibodies make Tg unreliable, and a raised Tg with a negative iodine scan calls for FDG-PET. Review the follow-up card.

secure.text: Secure: you ranked complications by frequency, matched voice and airway changes to the nerve, and put the clot first in a neck haematoma.

shaky.text: Shaky: most of the complications hold, but a nerve or order step slipped. Separate commonest from most feared, and pitch from hoarseness.

gap.text: Gap: complications are not settled. Hypocalcaemia is the commonest; unilateral RLN injury gives hoarseness, bilateral gives stridor, external SLN gives loss of pitch; a haematoma is opened at the bedside first. Review the complications card.

secure.text: Secure: you gave the AJCC age cut-off as 55 and placed the look-alikes correctly.

shaky.text: Shaky: the staging age and look-alikes mostly hold. Recheck that AJCC 8th uses 55, not 45.

gap.text: Gap: staging details are not holding. AJCC 8th uses 55 years, and under 55 there are only stages I and II. Review the staging card.

avoided.text: You separated 'first' from 'of choice'. TSH and ultrasound lead; FNAC names the nodule.

fell_recovered.text: You changed your mind on FNAC first and then held it on a later question. Keep reading whether the stem asks first or nature, since the old key can pull you back under time pressure.

fell_open.text: You treated 'investigation of choice' as 'first test', so FNAC or a scan came before TSH and ultrasound. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it again on a fresh question: review the work-up card, and read whether the stem asks first or nature.

avoided.text: You read the iodine qualifier. Papillary overall, follicular gaining share only in iodine deficiency.

fell_recovered.text: You moved off follicular as the default and read the setting later. Keep checking overall versus relative; stems can flip on one phrase.

fell_open.text: You stopped at 'most common' and ignored or inverted the setting, giving follicular. You may have fixed it on the spot. Meet it on a new question: review the iodine card, contrasting papillary overall with follicular in deficiency.

avoided.text: You knew FNAC reports Bethesda IV and that histology decides follicular carcinoma.

fell_recovered.text: You changed your mind about cytology or frozen section diagnosing follicular cancer. Under pressure the papillary habit of reading nuclei on FNAC can return, so keep asking what the test can see.

fell_open.text: You expected cytology or frozen section to name follicular carcinoma, carrying the papillary nuclei logic over. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it again on a fresh question: review the card on what FNAC and histology each answer; invasion is a histology finding.

avoided.text: You diagnosed papillary on nuclear features, not on papillae or psammoma bodies.

fell_recovered.text: You moved from papillae to nuclei as the test. Under exam pressure the name 'papillary' can pull you back, so check nuclei first.

fell_open.text: You defined papillary carcinoma by its architecture or by psammoma bodies, so a follicular pattern with ground-glass nuclei got called follicular. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the nuclei-decide card and the psammoma look-alikes.

avoided.text: You knew NIFTP is not a carcinoma.

fell_recovered.text: You moved from the old key to NIFTP. Under pressure the older 'follicular variant is cancer' answer can return, so ask whether invasion is present.

fell_open.text: You called a non-invasive follicular tumour with papillary-like nuclei a carcinoma, using the older key. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the NIFTP card, and check for invasion before calling cancer.

avoided.text: You gave the AJCC 8th cut-off as 55.

fell_recovered.text: You moved from 45 to 55. Under pressure the PYQ number can return, so ask which edition the stem uses.

fell_open.text: You used 45 years as the staging cut-off, the 7th edition value. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the staging card; AJCC 8th uses 55, and under 55 only stages I and II exist.

avoided.text: You chose surgery by size and risk, not one operation for all.

fell_recovered.text: You changed from one operation for every DTC to size and risk bands. Under pressure the classic total thyroidectomy key can return, so check size, nodes and extension.

fell_open.text: You applied total thyroidectomy to every differentiated cancer, ignoring size and risk. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the surgery ladder, with PYQs expecting total thyroidectomy and current guidance accepting lobectomy when low risk.

avoided.text: You read 'lateral aberrant thyroid' as nodal metastasis, not ectopia.

fell_recovered.text: You changed from ectopic thyroid to nodal metastasis. Under pressure the name can mislead again, so think by site: lateral neck, papillary node.

fell_open.text: You took the name literally and read a lateral neck mass of thyroid tissue as ectopic. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the card pairing lateral aberrant thyroid with papillary nodal metastasis.

avoided.text: You derived the routes correctly: papillary by lymphatics, follicular by blood.

fell_recovered.text: You reversed the routes at first, then held them. Under pressure, re-derive from invasion: follicular invades vessels, so it goes by blood.

fell_open.text: You held the two routes as a reversed pair, with follicular in lymphatics and papillary in blood. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the spread card, using vascular invasion as the cue for blood spread.

avoided.text: You built the site and DTC sets from logic. Nodes are uncommon in follicular, and medullary is not DTC.

fell_recovered.text: You dropped nodes from the follicular set and later held it. Under pressure the familiar item can creep back in, so test each against blood spread and follicular-cell origin.

fell_open.text: You added a familiar item to a set, counting cervical nodes as a usual follicular site or a non-DTC cancer as DTC. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the set-building card from follicular blood spread and follicular-cell origin.

avoided.text: You switched tests when Tg rose with a negative iodine scan.

fell_recovered.text: You moved from repeating the scan to FDG-PET. Under pressure, ask whether the tumour still takes up iodine.

fell_open.text: You trusted the negative scan or repeated it, instead of switching to a test that needs no iodine uptake. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the follow-up ladder, where a raised Tg with a negative scan points to radioiodine-refractory disease.

avoided.text: You stratified radioiodine by risk.

fell_recovered.text: You moved from radioiodine for all to radioiodine by risk. Under pressure 'standard adjuvant' can return, so check the ATA risk group.

fell_open.text: You treated radioiodine as routine for every DTC, dropping the risk qualifier. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the radioiodine card, contrasting low risk with high risk and metastasis.

avoided.text: You matched Bethesda II to follow-up, not surgery.

fell_recovered.text: You moved from operating on a benign report to follow-up. Under pressure, match category first, then action.

fell_open.text: You sent a benign cytology report to surgery. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the Bethesda card, where II means follow-up and surgery only for compression or cosmesis.

avoided.text: You kept Bethesda IV and V apart.

fell_recovered.text: You swapped IV and V at first, then separated them. Under pressure tie each number to its word: IV follicular neoplasm, V suspicious.

fell_open.text: You swapped Bethesda IV and V, recalling numbers without their word and action. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the Bethesda card, pairing IV with diagnostic lobectomy or molecular testing and V with cancer surgery.

avoided.text: You separated pitch change from hoarseness and chose the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.

fell_recovered.text: You moved from the recurrent laryngeal nerve to the external branch for pitch loss. Under pressure the familiar nerve can return, so link pitch to cricothyroid.

fell_open.text: You named the recurrent laryngeal nerve for loss of high pitch. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the nerve-to-symptom card, with cricothyroid and the external branch for pitch.

avoided.text: You separated commonest from most feared: hypocalcaemia is the commonest complication.

fell_recovered.text: You moved from nerve injury or bleeding to hypocalcaemia. Under pressure the dramatic complication can pull you back, so ask frequency.

fell_open.text: You ranked complications by how dramatic they are, picking nerve injury or bleeding as the commonest. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the complications card; transient hypocalcaemia is commonest, nerve injury is feared.

avoided.text: You opened the wound first for a neck haematoma.

fell_recovered.text: You moved from the airway device to releasing the clot first. Under pressure the intubate-first reflex can return, so ask what is compressing the airway.

fell_open.text: You went to the airway device before removing the clot compressing the airway. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the haematoma card, with bedside opening first and securing the airway after.

avoided.text: You kept the TSH phases apart: high before ablation, suppressed afterwards.

fell_recovered.text: You reversed the TSH direction at first, then separated the phases. Under pressure ask whether the phase needs uptake or tumour starvation.

fell_open.text: You suppressed TSH before radioiodine, applying the follow-up logic to the ablation phase. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the TSH card, where uptake needs high TSH before the dose and suppression follows.

avoided.text: You checked antibodies before trusting a low Tg.

fell_recovered.text: You moved from reading Tg alone to checking antibodies. Under pressure a low number can still reassure, so ask whether the assay can be trusted.

fell_open.text: You read a low thyroglobulin as reassuring without asking about anti-Tg antibodies. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the follow-up card; antibodies make Tg unreliable, so image and trend.

avoided.text: You paired each marker with its cell of origin.

fell_recovered.text: You swapped the markers at first, then separated them. Under pressure go by cell: follicular makes thyroglobulin, C cell makes calcitonin.

fell_open.text: You linked calcitonin to differentiated thyroid cancer, swapping the markers. You may have corrected it on the spot. Meet it on a fresh question: review the marker card; thyroglobulin follows DTC, calcitonin follows medullary carcinoma.

E1.text: You tend to confuse look-alikes: papillary architecture for papillary nuclei, or one laryngeal nerve for another. Before answering, name the one feature that separates the pair.

E2.text: You tend to add familiar items to a set, such as nodes to follicular spread or any thyroid cancer to DTC. Rebuild the set from its logic, then test each item against it.

E3.text: You tend to reverse a mechanism: spread routes or the TSH direction around radioiodine. Predict from the cause first, such as invasion of vessels meaning blood spread, then check.

E4.text: You tend to stretch 'most common' to mean the most dramatic. Read the exact qualifier: commonest, most feared and first-line are different questions.

E5.text: You tend to answer with the older PYQ key where current practice differs: FNAC first, total thyroidectomy for all, age 45, any follicular variant as cancer. Hold both: what PYQs expected and what is current.

E6.text: You tend to swap adjacent numbers or categories. Tie each number to its word and its action, then test yourself on the word first.

E7.text: You tend to miss the qualifier: iodine-deficient versus sufficient, low versus high risk, or antibodies present. Underline the qualifier in the stem before reading the options.

E8.text: You tend to pick a test that cannot answer the question asked: cytology for invasion, or a repeat scan for refractory disease. Ask what each test can see, then climb the ladder.

E9.text: You tend to get the order wrong: operating on a benign report or intubating before releasing a clot. Ask what comes first and why before choosing.

E10.text: You tend to pair a name or marker with the wrong condition: lateral aberrant thyroid as ectopia, or calcitonin with DTC. Pair by site and cell of origin instead of by label.

overconfident.text: You tapped Sure on at least two answers that were wrong. Those are the most useful errors, because a corrected confident error sticks best. Slow down on Sure answers and check the qualifier first.

underconfident.text: You tapped Guessing on several answers that were right. Your reasoning is better than you credit. When you can state why an option is right, tap Sure.

calibrated.text: Your Sure and Guessing taps tracked your accuracy. Keep that habit: it tells you which topics to review and which to leave.

hints_heavy.text: You asked for hints or explanations often. That is a sound strategy while learning, but cold recall is what the exam tests. Retake the module and try each probe before opening any help.

hints_none.text: You asked for no hints or explanations, so your falls were unaided errors. Next time, open the hint on the first miss; it is built to repair the wrong model without giving the answer.

hinted_only.text: In at least one area you were right only after a hint. That area is not yet secure. Review its card, then try it again without help.

fast_lane.text: You took a skip: the work-up detail, the follicular spread lesson, the Bethesda worked case or the follow-up worked case. Skipping is fine when you know it, but the skipped lesson is not tested for you. Check those review cards.

gap.text: Do the review cards in this order: confident errors first, then gaps, then shaky items. After each card, meet the idea again on a new question before moving on.

clear.text: No gaps showed. Space the review cards at 1, 3, 7, 21 and 60 days, and practise mixed 'first, most common, investigation of choice' stems.
